repo: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange is key-agnostic (takes raw key bytes) and is reusable verbatim for the shared-folder case without modification.
share_keys entries are keyed by itemId (file UUID), not by parent folder — file keys do NOT need re-registration after a folder move.
adoptSharedFolderResult must be called only once for the source result; calling it for the dest would corrupt the sharedFolderTree projection (dest is re-loaded on next navigateToSubfolder).
sdkCore.moveItem throws 'An item with this name already exists in destination' on collision — no auto-rename logic needed.
@internal on ensureFolderLoaded is documentation-only; CipherBoxClient is already exported, so direct calls from web are safe.
SharedFolderClient Pick allowlist (shared-folder-projection.ts:28-38) must be explicitly extended when adding new client methods — it only listed the 7 Phase 48 methods.
File IPNS key for re-encryption must be sourced from share_keys keyType:'file-ipns', NOT FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted (owner-wrapped; recipient cannot decrypt it).
Private-vault batch move is a web-layer pattern that loops single-item client.moveItem via useFileBrowserActions — there is no dedicated SDK batch method.
useSharedWriteOps.test.ts already exists; new handler unit tests should extend it rather than create a new file.
Intel API surface regeneration (gsd-tools regen intel) was a no-op — the regex extractor is unpopulated and produces an empty output.

code.finding: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange signature is fully key-agnostic; accepts raw sourceFolderKey/destFolderKey/fileIpnsPrivateKey bytes with no owner/recipient distinction.
sdkCore.moveItem throws on name collision — the error propagates through runWrite → p.setError with no auto-rename.
SharedFolderClient Pick allowlist — must add moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree when those methods are added to the client.
handleBatchMoveConfirm loops single-item moveItem calls using a selection Set; the private MoveDialog already accepts an items prop — batch shared move mirrors this pattern exactly.
handleDragStart is multi-select-aware; drop targets live on folder rows via handleDropOnFolder — the analog for SharedFolderRow DnD wiring.

workflow: GSD plan-phase flow: research → Nyquist VALIDATION.md → pattern-mapper → planner (opus) → plan-checker (sonnet) → revision loop until clean. One revision pass was needed here.
Sequential execution without worktrees was chosen for the AFK autonomous run to avoid the parallel-worktree merge-back protocol complexity (cwd-drift and merge-base footguns noted in project memory).
SDK dist must be explicitly rebuilt between waves when wave N adds new public SDK methods that wave N+1 imports — tsc checks the built dist, not source.
Web package has no typecheck npm script; the correct command is tsc -b run from the web package root.
gsd-tools is not on PATH inside planner-revision subagents — commits staged by those agents must be made manually by the orchestrator afterwards.

Scope expansion (batch + drag move) can be safely folded in mid-planning if the planner hasn't been spawned yet; ROADMAP and CONTEXT edits are committed before the planner runs so it picks them up cleanly.
User clarified that CodeRabbit CLI review runs before PR creation; after the PR is created CodeRabbit auto-posts a GitHub review, which is then addressed via /resolve-pr-reviews.
